title: Shell許可ルールの解釈が実際のシェル意味論とずれ、書いた権限境界と実効境界が一致しない
summary: Agent harnesses match Bash allow/deny rules lexically against a command string, while the shell that executes it has richer semantics. In this window both vendors patched divergences: Claude Code auto-approved arithmetic assignments such as OPTIND=1/0, mis-handled dangling && / || operators, and warned that an allow rule like Bash(git * main) also matches arbitrary options; Codex began requiring approval for commands containing dynamic shell words. The failure is silent - the operator believes a narrow rule is in force while a crafted or merely malformed command slips past the classifier. Unlike a harness vulnerability, the remediation lands on the user: every hand-written Bash allow rule predating 2026-08-20 must be re-audited, not just upgraded past.

evidence.title: claude-code CHANGELOG v2.1.251 / v2.1.246 / v2.1.238
evidence.summary: v2.1.251 'Fixed Bash permission checks auto-approving commands that assign an arithmetic expression to an integer shell variable (e.g. OPTIND=1/0)'; v2.1.246 'always require approval for malformed commands with a dangling && or || operator' plus a startup warning that wildcard-before-subcommand allow rules 'also match options'; v2.1.238 improved checking for zsh-specific conditional syntax.

evidence.title: ChatGPT & Codex changelog, 2026-08-20
evidence.summary: 'Require approval for commands with dynamic shell words' - independent vendor patching the same class of allowlist evasion in the same window.

notes: Checked I03 (permissions granted too broadly), I12 (approval fatigue), I16 (harness vulnerability), I17 (agent bypasses normal process). I03 assumes the grant itself is wide; here the grant is correctly narrow and the matcher is wrong. I16 is the closest but its practical response is 'upgrade the agent', whereas this requires auditing user-authored allow rules whose meaning was never what the author intended. Two independent vendors in one 21-day window supports treating it as a class.
